title: Reversing soil salinization
bottleneck: Salinization affects 160 million hectares of cropland and renders 1.5 million hectares unproductive every year, driven by irrigation in arid regions — the very regions most dependent on irrigation. Reversal requires leaching with large volumes of fresh water, which is scarce where salinization occurs, plus drainage infrastructure: an expensive combination. Salt-tolerant varieties help at the margins but don't restore degraded land.
why_it_blocks: Irrigated drylands are among the world's most productive farmland. Losing 1.5M hectares yearly to salt is a slow amputation of the food supply. Irrigated drylands are among the world's most productive farmland; losing them to salt is a slow amputation.
current_state: FAO's Global Map of Salt-Affected Soils guides targeting across 118 countries; large-scale reclamation projects are rare and costly.
